title: Vandal sack of Rome
summary: In June 455 CE, King Gaiseric's Vandals landed from Carthage and thoroughly plundered Rome for fourteen days following the assassination of Emperor Petronius Maximus. Pope Leo I negotiated an entry without slaughter, but the Vandals stripped the city's wealth, temples, and palaces and took thousands of captives.

uncertainty.note: Chronicler Prosper dates entry to 2 June 455 for 14 days; Mathisen notes some sources suggest late May 455.

as_recorded.calendar: Julian (Victor of Tonnena / modern scholarly encyclopedia)
as_recorded.value: fourteen whole days denuded the city of all its riches and took with him the daughters and wife of Valentinian
plundered also the temple of Jupiter Capitolinus

importance.justification: The fourteen-day systematic stripping of Rome's monumental wealth and capture of the imperial family left the western empire powerless and fiscally ruined.

related.because: Vandal control of Carthage provided the naval base and maritime fleet to attack Rome.

beats.caption: In June 455, Gaiseric's Vandals systematically plunder Rome's palaces and temples over fourteen days.
The Vandals carry off Rome's treasure and the imperial family to Carthage, crippling the Western empire.
